reason: Continue the supporting-material branch by supplying amino acids to the collagen-producing cells.

reason: Continue the supporting-material branch by bringing the collagen-producing cells together with extracellular fluid.

reason: Start the muscle branch using the only available combination.

reaction: The contrast with the collagen branch makes selective gene activity clear.
reason: Use the only available combination to supply building blocks for muscle proteins.
expectation: I expect the cells to make muscle proteins; further development may be needed to form mature fibres.

effect: The muscle branch produced separate myoblasts with muscle proteins, completing the goal without implying they are mature fibres.
reaction: The distinction between precursors and fused muscle fibres is useful, and the shared amino-acid supply ties the branches together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building collagen-rich extracellular matrix was most worthwhile: the planned sequence connects gene activity and protein production to material that supports cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The muscle branch repeated the differentiation-then-amino-acid pattern, making its choices less engaging, though the comparison reinforced the biology.

surprise.text: The final result stopped at separate myoblasts rather than producing mature muscle fibres, making the developmental limit explicit.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though combining extracellular fluid with fibroblasts was an abstract way to represent secretion and assembly rather than an obvious physical operation.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the contrast between cell lineages and the unfinished development of muscle make me curious about what comes next.
